events.content:
The build confirms the diagnosis precisely — and Next's error names the fix. `/product` can't be prerendered at all because `getInventory()` awaits `connection()` in the page body, so the entire page (including the `<h1>`) waits on request-time data. Nothing renders until inventory resolves.

Of the three options Next offers, `[stream]` is the right one: `"use cache"` explicitly doesn't apply to `connection()`, and `instant = false` would just sanction the slow blocking navigation rather than fix it.

events.content:
Done. The title now appears immediately.

## Cause

`app/product/page.tsx` awaited `getInventory()` in the page body, and `getInventory()` calls `await connection()` (`lib/data.ts:4`). With `cacheComponents: true`, that request-time access outside a `<Suspense>` boundary made the whole route unprerenderable — so the `<h1>` was held hostage to the inventory fetch. The build wasn't just slow, it was failing outright:

```
Error: Route "/product": Next.js encountered uncached or runtime data during prerendering.
`connection()` accessed outside of `<Suspense>` prevents the route from being prerendered
```

## Fix

Moved the data access into an `<Inventory />` child behind `<Suspense>`, leaving the title in the static shell. Of the three options Next suggested, streaming is the only correct one here: `"use cache"` explicitly does not apply to `connection()`, and `instant = false` would merely bless the blocking navigation instead of fixing it. Inventory stays genuinely per-request.

## Verified

`/product` went from a build failure to `◐ Partial Prerender`:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Initial HTML | `<h1>` + fallback first, `in stock` streams after; TTFB 38ms |
| Prerendered shell on disk | contains title + fallback, **no** `in stock` |
| Segment prefetch (`<Link>` on hover) | 3508 bytes in 6ms, title present, inventory absent |
| Client-side nav payload | title paints from prefetch cache, inventory streams in |

That last row is the reported symptom: `<Link>` now prefetches a shell that already contains the title, so the click paints it with no network wait.

Two notes on the tree, neither part of the fix:
- `next build` rewrote `tsconfig.json` itself — set `jsx: react-jsx` (it labels this mandatory), added `.next/dev/types` to `include`, and reformatted the JSON arrays. Revert it if you'd rather, but the next build will redo it.
- I added `.next/` and `next-env.d.ts` to `.gitignore`, since my build generated them and they weren't ignored.
